newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS UPDATE - MAY 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS UPDATE - MAY 26.

text.p: --The downward course of drachma interest rates and the developments on international money markets with the yen and dollar are causing headaches at the finance ministry and problems for businesses wanting to take out foreign exchange loans.

--The government is not considering the abolition of bonus wages or the way they are paid, according to sources close to National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou, following press reports over the weekend.
--Xiosbank shares go on sale at the Athens Stock Exchange today.

--The government is planning a new package of economic measures to meet convergence programme goals that aim at reducing the public deficit and inflation. The measures include the sale of major stakes in state-run banks as well as the distribution of holiday bonuses to be paid out over a 12-month period.

--Reports say the Bank of Greece is looking at additional measures to protect the portfolios of banks in an effort to strengthen the supervisory role of credit institutions. The move is connected to a 1996 study which said many institutions had a less than satisfactory portfolio performance, high operating costs and non-existent organisational and technological structures.

--The Athens bourse is becoming a magnet for informatics companies with four firms - Sysware, Info Quest, European Dynamic, and DIS - showing interest in being listed. The main reason for the interest is attributed to the need for cheap capital to investments in the rapidly-growing sector.
--The second international Intertank forum gets under way on Monday in Athens with the participation of shipping companies, experts and government officials.

--The recent closure of 75-year-old Akron Ilion Krystal sent shockwaves through the Greek high street even though it was expected. Apart from the foodstuffs 'superstars' of the retail trade, thousands of small and medium size retailers and four major companies - Dragonas, Katrantzos, Diamantis and Akron - have closed their doors since 1980. Changing consumer trends have also forced other major names such as Minion, Klaoudatos, Lambropoulos to change their tack.

--Under the shadow of a recent spate of reports on the Greek economy on the need for structural changes to the economy, social dialogue between the government, unions and employers is expected to begin tackling the heart of the issues within the week.

--The timetable for Greek telecoms organisation OTE's second share off on the stock market is firming up: Public subscription is expected to begin on June 11-13 and book building for institutional investors on June 91-13. Thousands of Greeks and foreign small investors and more than 500 institutional investors from Greece and abroad will bid for the shares. Prices will range from 6,000-6,500 drachmas.

--The government is preparing a new package of measures under the pressure of social dialogue and coming municipal elections. The reports say that the special charge on cars will be abolished, taxes on alcohol and cigarettes will be reduced and the tax scale adjusted for inflation by 5.0 percent and the tax-free threshold increased. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
